A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIV‐1 RNA copy number in plasma is not necessarily correlated with infectivity.
the early phase of AZT treatment is characterized by transient dissociations between infectious HIV‐1 titers, HIV RNA copy numbers and p‐24‐antigen levels.
the HIV‐1 RNA copy number does not always correlate with infectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a dissociation between the number of HIV particles and their ability to cause infection.
the HIV RNA level does not always correlate with infectivity, and that there are other factors at play in the viral load of an HIV patient.
the use of plasma HIV‐1 RNA levels as a surrogate for infectivity is problematic.
